episodes.169579: Shortwave moved through the southwesterly flow aloft that's been parked over the area this week and set off another round of severe thunderstorms over the area this afternoon into the overnight hours.
episodes.169593: Another active monsoon day impacted northern New Mexico on July 8, 2022, as thunderstorms developed across the mountainous terrain by early afternoon and becoming more widespread through the evening. Strong thunderstorms with heavy rainfall on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused Tecolote Creek to exceed its banks, flooding area roadways. Meanwhile, a thunderstorm near Raton interacted with a boundary to briefly produce quarter size hail.
episodes.169594: As moisture values remained abnormally high across northern and central New Mexico on July 9, 2022, it was another busy monsoon day as numerous thunderstorms impacted the area. These thunderstorms were generally sub-severe with no flash flooding reports received, however, a strong thunderstorms with a likely wet microburst in Albuquerque produced nickel size hail and a 58 mph wind gust.
episodes.169677: Lightning struck and killed a man why floating down a river in Brewton.
episodes.169744: Very hot temperatures on the afternoon of the eighth allowed for isolated thunderstorms to develop on the South Plains. Thunderstorms initially developed on an outflow boundary draped across the extreme southern Texas Panhandle that developed from early morning thunderstorms in the Texas Panhandle. A relatively dry sub-cloud layer enhanced the downburst potential of these storms. A few of these storms were able to produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.169751: A weak cold front slowly moved through the area later on the 8th into the 9th. A wave of low pressure tracked along the front, passing through the area during that time. Plenty of moisture ahead of the boundary along with moderate instability led to areas of heavy rainfall. The slower storm motion and training storms led to areas of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169752: A weak cold front slowly moved through the area later on the 8th into the 9th. A wave of low pressure tracked along the front, passing through the area during that time. Plenty of moisture ahead of the boundary along with moderate instability led to areas of heavy rainfall. The slower storm motion and training storms led to areas of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169753: A weak cold front slowly moved through the area later on the 8th into the 9th. A wave of low pressure tracked along the front, passing through the area during that time. Plenty of moisture ahead of the boundary along with moderate instability led to areas of heavy rainfall. The slower storm motion and training storms led to areas of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169817: Diurnal heating led to scattered thunderstorms, a couple of which produced wind damage.
episodes.170053: Disturbances moved through a persistent southwest flow aloft across the region, which continued to provide daily afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. These storms, some of which were severe, brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, heavy localized rainfall, and lightning.
episodes.170703: Scattered intense thunderstorms fired up during the heat of the day across southern Illinois. This activity developed ahead of a weak cold front and in the vicinity of a weak surface low centered over the mid Mississippi Valley. The atmosphere was quite unstable, with mixed-layer capes from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Wind shear was sufficiently strong for isolated storms to become severe, with damaging wind gusts. Effective bulk shear was around 30 to 35 knots.
episodes.170704: Scattered intense thunderstorms fired up during the heat of the day across southwest Indiana. This activity developed ahead of a weak cold front and surface low centered over the mid Mississippi Valley. The atmosphere was quite unstable, with mixed-layer capes from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Wind shear was sufficiently strong for an isolated storm to become severe, with large hail. Effective bulk shear was around 30 to 35 knots.
episodes.170705: Scattered intense thunderstorms fired up during the heat of the day across western Kentucky. This activity developed ahead of a weak cold front and in the vicinity of a weak surface low centered over the mid Mississippi Valley. The atmosphere was quite unstable, with mixed-layer capes from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Wind shear was sufficiently strong for isolated storms to become severe, with damaging wind gusts. Effective bulk shear was around 30 to 35 knots. The storms maintained intensity through the evening and early night-time hours. Weak steering winds aloft contributed to slow storm movement and an isolated flash flood.
episodes.170706: Scattered intense thunderstorms fired up during the heat of the day across southeast Missouri. This activity developed along a weak cold front and in the vicinity of a weak surface low centered over the mid Mississippi Valley. The atmosphere was quite unstable, with mixed-layer capes from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Wind shear was sufficiently strong for an isolated storm to become severe, with damaging wind gusts. Effective bulk shear was around 30 to 35 knots.
episodes.171016: A complex of thunderstorms erupted during the mid afternoon hours over northwest and north central Alabama, then sliding southeast into central Alabama.  The thunderstorms produced several reports of wind damage.
episodes.171044: A broken line of thunderstorms moved through the area from the north on the evening of July 9th. These storms resulted in numerous instances of damaging winds that brought down trees and power lines mainly along and north of I-20.
episodes.171478: A supercell thunderstorm developed across southwestern Weston County and tracked northeast across portions of the county before weakening as it moved into South Dakota. The storm produced large hail in some locations, including the Newcastle area.
episodes.171583: A weak low pressure system was located in southwestern Illinois on the afternoon of July 8, 2022, with a stationary front draped near the I-70 corridor. A secondary cold front pushed into central Illinois from the north, and scattered thunderstorms developed along both boundaries. As storm clusters progressed to the southeast, they produced isolated flash flooding, hail, and wind damage.
episodes.171681: A broken line of thunderstorms developed and moved across southeast South Carolina in the afternoon hours. A few portions of the line of thunderstorms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171682: A strong line of thunderstorms developed near the southeast Georgia coast and steadily progressed to the east and northeast along the southeast South Carolina coast. The thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the coastline.
episodes.171792: A cold front moved through the region, triggering showers and storms. Some of the storms became severe producing damaging winds.
episodes.171949: Above average moisture for early July combined with areawide lift from a short-wave was able to produce multiple storms capable of severe hail.
episodes.171965: Several rounds of severe weather occurred during the July 9-13 time frame. These rounds of thunderstorms were the result of two cold fronts moving across the state in association with a surface low moving along the boundary.
episodes.171984: On July 8th, an evening severe thunderstorm developed in northwestern Kansas due to daytime heating. This thunderstorm produced a 63 mph wind gust.
episodes.171986: Thunderstorms moved into western North Dakota from Montana as a low level jet increased in intensity. Early in the episode, a thunderstorm produced severe winds over McKenzie County. Later on in the episode, additional storms became severe over south central North Dakota. The strongest wind gust reported was 62 mph near Mandan in Morton County. The largest hail reported was one inch in diameter, occurring near Braddock in Emmons County.
episodes.172009: A late season cold front pushed southward across Central Alabama on July 9th.  The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable with afternoon surface based CAPE of 4000-4500 J/kg and lifted indices around -7 Celsius.  PWAT's were above two inches which also supported heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.172036: A few isolated storms formed along a weak boundary in northern North Carolina, which resulted in a few downed trees in Yadkin and Wilkes counties.
episodes.172042: A cold front moved south across the Mid-South. Convection initiated along and south of the boundary which by the afternoon was over north Mississippi. Storms produced damaging wind and heavy rainfall.
episodes.172077: A cold front moved south across the Mid-South. Convection developed along the boundary as it moved across northwest Tennessee. Storms produced damaging wind and heavy rainfall.
episodes.172090: Sufficient CAPE, SHEAR, dew points in the upper 50s, and southwest flow combined to produce severe weather.
episodes.172158: The proximity of an induced trough, along with an upper level trough generated unsettled weather conditions along the area. A waterspout was reported west of Rincon.
episodes.172170: A weak frontal boundary which sagged south through the I-20 corridor provided focus for isolated thunderstorm development on the afternoon of Saturday July 9. Triple digit temperatures that afternoon provided sufficient instability for severe downburst winds in a few of these storms.
episodes.172293: Strong thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and produced gusty winds that caused damage in southwest Alabama.
episodes.172299: The center of a dominant upper-level ridge retrograded slightly westward over the Rockies, allowing a weak shortwave trough to advance southeast across the Southern Plains into the Ark-La-Tex region. This trough was accompanied by a weak frontal boundary at the surface, moving south from Oklahoma and Arkansas and eventually south of the Red River by late afternoon in the evening hours. Ahead of the boundary, temperatures in the triple digits combined with a very unstable air mass and precipitable water values near two inches. This resulted in elevated thunderstorms developing within the unstable air mass, where isolated damaging wind gusts were produced from a few severe thunderstorms across portions of Northeast Texas during the late afternoon and early evening.
episodes.172310: Slow moving thunderstorms produced extremely heavy rain that caused flooding in Mobile county.
episodes.172357: Surface high pressure to the southeast and a front approaching southeast Georgia resulted in west-southwesterly steering flow. The combination of diurnal heating, ample moisture and convergence ahead of the frontal boundary led to numerous showers and storms developing in NE FL. With west-southwest flow, the east coast sea breeze was pinned along the Atlantic coast. Pre-frontal storms moving east-southeastward interacted with the pinned boundary as they shifted into the Atlantic causing a brief waterspout off the coast of Huguenot park.
episodes.172358: Surface high pressure to the southeast and a front approaching southeast Georgia resulted in west-southwesterly steering flow. The combination of diurnal heating, ample moisture and convergence ahead of the frontal boundary led to numerous showers and storms developing in NE FL. With west-southwest flow, the east coast sea breeze was pinned along the Atlantic coast as the dominant west coast sea breeze shifted inland in the afternoon. Isolated strong storms developed along the sea breeze boundary collision producing gusts of 40 to 45 mph and knocking a large tree down across SR 11 in Flagler county.
episodes.172371: Isolated late afternoon thunderstorms developed across the Concho Valley and Heartland due to moderate instability and hot temperatures. A few storms were severe and caused wind damage and hail.
episodes.172494: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region.  There were a few reports of flooding and trees down across southwest Georgia.
episodes.172567: Afternoon thunderstorms formed across portions of the Texas Panhandle on the afternoon of the 8th due to instability and wind shear in the atmosphere. As a result, severe thunderstorms developed with reports of large hail and wind damage due to severe wind gusts.
episodes.172601: A very warm and humid air mass south of an approaching backdoor front combined with passing mid level disturbances within a broad mid-level trough to produce widespread showers and storms. Very high moisture, deeply warm low levels, and slow storm motion produced high rainfall rates and flash flooding, ranging from nuisance flooding in most places to road closures in Chapel Hill, Durham, and Wake county. Isolated damaging winds were also reported in Sampson County.
episodes.172631: Scattered showers and thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of the Virginia Northern Neck and Middle Peninsula.
episodes.172636: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.172639: An area of 1 to 2 inches of rainfall occurred across the headwaters of the Little Sioux River on July 5 and resulted in a brief period of minor to locally moderate flooding.
episodes.172651: Isolated thunderstorm associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.172941: Scattered storms and storm clusters moved across the North Carolina Piedmont during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Union County.
episodes.172984: Scattered thunderstorms once again affected Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of July 8 into the early morning hours on July 9. Several reports of wind damage were received.
episodes.173067: Typical afternoon summertime showers and thunderstorms developed within a persistent and abnormally moist tropical airmass during the afternoon and evening of July 8th , aided by stout instability as a weak upper level disturbance moved around the eastern periphery of a retrograding upper level ridge. These storms produced numerous reports of trees and powerlines down and isolated flash flooding across portions of north Georgia and far east-central Georgia.
